title: Story Archetypes (Jungian, via the Campbell/Vogler synthesis)
source: C.G. Jung (archetypes) synthesized into 8 story functions (cf. Vogler, The Writer's Journey)
license: labels/idea only; Vogler's descriptive prose is copyright and NOT reproduced — descriptions authored for monomyth
tier_note: A character-archetype facet, orthogonal to Propp role and Greimas actant. Archetypes are function-flexible (a Shapeshifter can occupy Helper or Opponent), giving the generator controlled ambiguity and twist potential.

items.name: Hero
items.description: The protagonist the audience identifies with; grows by facing and overcoming the central ordeal.

items.name: Mentor
items.description: Guides, teaches, and gifts the hero; embodies the hero's higher self or accumulated wisdom.

items.name: Threshold Guardian
items.description: Tests the hero's resolve at the boundary between worlds; an obstacle to be overcome, absorbed, or turned into an ally.

items.name: Herald
items.description: Announces the call to adventure and signals that change is coming; sets the story in motion.

items.name: Shapeshifter
items.description: Ambiguous and unstable in loyalty or identity; keeps the hero (and audience) uncertain of their true nature.

items.name: Shadow
items.description: The antagonist or repressed dark side; embodies the hero's fears and the forces to be defeated or integrated.

items.name: Ally
items.description: Companion who accompanies, aids, and complements the hero through the journey.

items.name: Trickster
items.description: Agent of mischief and change; provides comic relief and punctures pretension, catalyzing transformation.
